description: These are the foundations underneath almost everything a software engineer does.

subjects.title: Mathematics for Computer Science
description: Mathematics is particularly important for algorithms, graphics, AI, cryptography, scientific computing and quantum computing.

description: You should understand the different ways programs can be designed.

subjects.title: Programming Languages and Ecosystem
description: A software engineer does not need to master every programming language. However, you should understand the major language families and know which types of problems they solve.

subjects.title: Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA)
description: This area should be studied from simple structures to advanced algorithmic techniques.

subjects.title: Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC)
description: A professional engineer needs to understand the entire life of a software product, not just writing code.

Quantum Computing
description: This is a substantial specialization of its own. It is not just another programming framework.

groups.title: Closely related but distinct: post-quantum cryptography

closing_notes: One important distinction: quantum computing uses quantum hardware to process certain classes of problems; post-quantum cryptography uses conventional computers to implement cryptographic methods designed to resist quantum attacks.

IBM's published roadmap, for example, discusses quantum error-correction development, hybrid quantum-classical workflows and fault-tolerant systems as milestones in the 2026–2030 period. These are company targets, not guaranteed delivery dates.

closing_notes: AI tools can accelerate engineering work, but understanding the system and validating the output remain essential.
